newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZCCM sale opens up Zambia drilling chances.
newsitem.headline: ZCCM sale opens up Zambia drilling chances.

text.p: Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines' (ZCCM) privatisation had opened investment opportunities which had resulted in over $22 million being committed to drilling projects so far, the Investment Centre said on Friday.

"Since the sale of the mines began, opportunities for investments in drilling projects have increased with drilling in Konkola North, Kansanshi, Konkola Deep, Luanshya basin, Luanshya and Nchanga totalling over $22 million," an investment centre spokesman told Reuters.
The spokesman said a Botswana-based drilling company had been awarded $15 million contracts with the newly privatised Konkola North and Kansanshi mines.
The centre said it issued Boart Longyear Africa Ltd, a subsidiary of Boart Drilling (Pty) Ltd of Botswana, with an investment license to carry out the projects.

"So far, the company has been awarded a 20-month drilling contract by Anglovaal Ltd worth $10 million and a $5 million contract with Cyprus Amax to handle Konkola North and Kansashi," an investment centre spokesman said.

Avmin Ltd, the mineral division of Anglovaal, signed an option agreement on the development of Konkola North mine in March. The company aims to delineate not less than 100 million tonnes at copper grade adequate to support the economic exploitation of ore at depths of up to 1,500 metres.

Cyprus Amax Minerals Co bought 80 percent of Kansanshi mine, the first ZCCM mine to be privatised in January. The company estimates Kansanshi to have a reserve grade of around 1.5 percent copper with a material amount of gold as a by-product.
Other ZCCM assets are due for privatisation by the end of the year.
A ZCCM spokesman said this week negotiations with six bidders for the mining conglomerate's assets were going ahead as planned. --Lusaka newsroom +2601 222-689
